program_name: Computer Science (English-language track of the Bachelor's Degree in Informatica / Computer Science, University of Trento)
teaching_language: English. Case (2) in the classification: the L-31 degree programme exists as two parallel tracks (percorsi) under one official Italian degree - 'Informatica (track in Italian language)' and 'Computer Science (track in English language)'. The English track has been offered since a.y. 2024/2025 and is delivered entirely in English (the programme card states 'You can take the course in Italian or English' and 'LANGUAGE: English Italian' because both tracks are listed together on the same page). The year-1 study plan of the English track includes a compulsory 0-CFU 'Language Test: English B2' plus a 3-CFU 'Choice of language' slot in which non-Italian speakers normally take 'Italian language (A1)' - this is a language service course, not a sign that content teaching is in Italian. Non-native Italian speakers enrolled in the English track must also pass a basic Italian language proficiency test before taking 3rd-year exams.
campus: Trento - Polo Ferrari 1 (Povo campus), via Sommarive 5, 38123 Povo (TN), Department of Information Engineering and Computer Science (DISI)
admission_type: Restricted access / numero programmato ('ACCESS: Programmed'). Selection is by ranking list based on a CISIA test: TOLC-I or CEnT-S (CISIA English Test - Sciences). For a.y. 2026/2027 the English track is entered via TOLC-I (EU and equivalent candidates, all three sessions) or via CEnT-S (first session only; compulsory for non-EU candidates, optional for EU and equivalent candidates). Three admission sessions for EU/equivalent candidates; non-EU candidates residing abroad may apply only in the first session.
academic_requirements: 1) Educational qualification: an Italian secondary school diploma ('diploma di maturita') or an equivalent foreign qualification, already held or to be obtained by 31 July 2026. A foreign qualification must have been obtained after at least 12 years of schooling, after attending the final two years of the foreign education system concerned, and must give access to a comparable university programme in the issuing country; where the issuing country requires an academic suitability test for university entry, proof of passing it is required (examples explicitly listed in the call: Selectividad in Spain, Gaokao in China, Prova de Afericao / Prova Geral de Acesso ao Ensino Superior in Portugal, YKS in Turkey, Konkur in Afghanistan). 2) Test requirement: pass the TOLC-I or CEnT-S within the validity windows of the chosen session (test taken in calendar year 2025 or 2026). 3) Age: non-EU candidates only must have reached the age of majority by 30 September 2026. 4) Seats for a.y. 2026/2027, Computer Science (English track), total 105: 1st session 70 seats = 27 for EU and equivalent with TOLC-I + 18 for EU and equivalent with CEnT-S + 25 reserved for non-EU candidates with CEnT-S; 2nd session 25 seats (EU and equivalent, TOLC-I only); 3rd session 10 seats (EU and equivalent, TOLC-I only). Unassigned first-session places roll over to later sessions. 5) Minimum eligibility thresholds: 18/50 on the TOLC-I; 16/45 on the CEnT-S. Only in the third session, TOLC-I scores of 17 to below 18 are admitted with OFA (Additional Learning Requirements). 6) No GPA threshold and no bachelor-field prerequisite apply (this is a first-cycle programme). 7) Tie-breaking: TOLC-I - higher Mathematics section, then Sciences section, then younger candidate; CEnT-S - higher Mathematics section, then 'Reasoning on texts and data' section, then younger candidate. 8) Non-EU merit benefits: the CEnT-S score is converted to a /100 scale (16/45 equated to 50/100); candidates scoring at least 70/100 who rank highly may be awarded a scholarship (number of scholarships per programme announced together with the ranking).
language_requirements: English (English curriculum): B2 level, 'which you need to acquire or certify during the admission process or at the latest before taking exams belonging to the 2nd and 3rd year'. The year-1 study plan contains a compulsory 0-CFU 'Language Test: English B2' (code COCS_EN_B2). The admission call adds that students admitted to Computer Science (English track) 'must pass an English proficiency exam at the level required by the Degree Program Regulations within their first year of study'. No specific IELTS/TOEFL score is published as a hard admission gate: proficiency can be demonstrated by (a) taking and passing the English test at the University Language Centre (CLA) before the start of the second year, or (b) submitting, after enrolment, a recognised international language certificate at a level equal to or higher than the required level (list of accepted certificates published by CLA). Free CLA language courses are available. Certificate recognition is requested through the online application 'Language certificates - Departments of Physics, Information Engineering and Computer Science, Industrial Engineering, Mathematics, CIBIO' on webapps.unitn.it. Additional requirements specific to the English curriculum: native Italian speakers must reach English C1 or Technical English before taking 3rd-year exams; non-native Italian speakers must pass a basic Italian language proficiency test before taking 3rd-year exams (an Italian language A1 course worth 3 CFU is offered in the year-1 'Choice of language' slot). Note: the English section at the end of the TOLC-I does not count towards the admission score and, for the English track, does not substitute the B2 requirement (that substitution route is stated only for the Italian curriculum). For comparison, the Italian curriculum requires English A2 then B1.
application_deadline_eu: A.Y. 2026/2027, three sessions for EU and equivalent candidates: 1st session - admission application from mid-December 2025 to 23 March 2026, 12:00 (TOLC-I taken between 1 January 2025 and 20 March 2026; CEnT-S between 1 November 2025 and 31 March 2026); 2nd session - application from 9 April to 11 May 2026, 12:00 (TOLC-I between 1 January 2025 and 8 May 2026); 3rd session - application from 4 June to 31 July 2026, 12:00 (test by 29-31 July 2026). Rankings: by 2 April 2026 (TOLC-I) and by 6 April 2026 (CEnT-S) for session 1, by 20 May 2026 for session 2, by 6-7 August 2026 for session 3. Educational qualification confirmation for sessions 1 and 2: 6-17 July 2026, 12:00.
application_deadline_non_eu: A.Y. 2026/2027: first session only - admission application by 23 March 2026, 12:00. CEnT-S must be taken between November 2025 and 31 March 2026 (UniTrento accepts normalised scores available by 30 January for the 1st macro-period and by 31 March for the 2nd macro-period). Non-EU ranking published by 6 April 2026 per the call PDF / by 14 April 2026 per the programme webpage. Pre-enrolment by the deadline stated in the ranking (non-refundable EUR 80 fee); educational qualification confirmation 6-17 July 2026; embassy/consulate pre-enrolment on Universitaly for the study visa; the entry visa must be obtained no later than 31 October 2026 and the student must be in Italy by the start of classes.
required_documents: [uncertain] UniTrento does not publish a single consolidated document checklist for this programme; the documents named in the 2026/27 admission call and linked pages are: (1) identification/authentication for the online application - SPID, CIE (Italian electronic ID) or a UniTrento account; non-EU applicants and applicants without an Italian tax code/ID must register a UniTrento 'guest' account at least three working days before the deadline; (2) CISIA test registration and completed TOLC-I or CEnT-S (results are retrieved automatically by UniTrento from the CISIA database - no document upload by the candidate); (3) for candidates with a foreign qualification (uploaded during the online application, .pdf or .jpg): if the final qualification is not yet obtained, a Transcript of Records with subjects and grades for the last two years of study; if already obtained, a scanned copy of the diploma - a certified translation into Italian or English is required unless the document is in English, French, German or Spanish; (4) if the qualification was obtained after fewer than 12 years of schooling, the documentation listed in Attachment 1 of the Italian Ministry's 'Annual procedures for entry, residency and enrolment of international students'; (5) if the issuing country requires an academic suitability test for university admission, scanned proof of having passed it; (6) UniTrento may additionally request a CIMEA Statement of Verification and/or Statement of Comparability; (7) candidates with disabilities or SLD: certification uploaded through the CISIA document upload form (foreign certifications must be accompanied by an Italian or English translation); (8) after enrolment, optional English language certificate for recognition of the B2 requirement, submitted through the CLA/webapps online form. Payments: TOLC-I registration EUR 35.00 or CEnT-S registration EUR 55.00 to CISIA; the UniTrento admission application itself is free; pre-enrolment fee EUR 80 (non-refundable).
entry_exam_or_test: CISIA admission test, no UniTrento-specific exam and no interview. Two routes for a.y. 2026/2027: (a) TOLC-I - national CISIA test, 50 scored questions (Mathematics 20, Logic 10, Sciences 10, Verbal comprehension 10; 110 min) plus a compulsory but unscored 30-question English section (15 min); can be taken in person (TOLC@UNI) at any CISIA university or online (TOLC@HOME); fee EUR 35.00; may be repeated but not more than once per calendar month; minimum threshold 18/50; valid for the English track in all three sessions. (b) CEnT-S (CISIA English Test - Sciences) - English-language CISIA test used specifically for DISI's English-taught programmes; 55 questions of which UniTrento scores 45 (Mathematics 15, Reasoning on texts and data 15, Chemistry 10, Physics 5 - the 10 Biology questions are excluded), 90 min; taken in person (CEnT@UNI) or from home (CEnT@CASA); fee EUR 55.00; can be taken once per macro-period (macro-period 1: Nov-Dec 2025 and Jan 2026; macro-period 2: Feb-Mar 2026); scores are normalised and published at the end of each macro-period; minimum threshold 16/45; valid for the first session only; MANDATORY for non-EU candidates and OPTIONAL for EU and equivalent candidates. Scoring for both tests: +1 correct, 0 unanswered, -0.25 incorrect. Note: for a.y. 2026/2027 the call no longer lists 'English TOLC-I' as an admission route for the English track - it has been replaced by the CEnT-S.

uncertainty_notes: 1) SOURCE ACCESS: corsi.unitn.it returns HTTP 405 and www.unitn.it returns HTTP 403 to direct automated requests (WAF/Cloudflare). All corsi.unitn.it and www.unitn.it content above was retrieved through a plain-text rendering proxy of the same official URLs, and the 2026/27 admission call PDF was read in full (24 pages) that way; www.disi.unitn.it and webapps.unitn.it were reachable directly. Facts were cross-checked between the call PDF, the English programme page and its Italian twin page. 2) ENTRY TEST CHANGE vs. THE TASK BRIEF: the brief said admission is via 'English TOLC-I (CISIA)'. That was true for a.y. 2025/26; for a.y. 2026/2027 the DISI call no longer lists an English TOLC-I for the English track - the English-language route is now the CEnT-S (CISIA English Test - Sciences), first session only, mandatory for non-EU and optional for EU candidates, while EU candidates may alternatively sit the (Italian) TOLC-I in any of the three sessions. Anyone comparing against 2025/26 material will see the older wording. 3) INCONSISTENCY BETWEEN OFFICIAL PAGES: the English admission page lists under the first session 'Italian proficiency test for Non-Europeans: 11 March 2026'; the Italian version of the same page (corsi.unitn.it/it/informatica-laurea/iscriversi/ammissione-e-immatricolazione) does not contain that line, and the 2026/27 call makes no Italian-language requirement for admission to the English track. It is most likely a leftover/template item, but it could not be reconciled - treat it as unverified. 4) RANKING PUBLICATION DATE MISMATCH: the call PDF states the non-EU first-session ranking is published 'by April 6, 2026', while the programme webpage says 'by 14 April 2026'; the Italian binding version of the call would settle this. Similarly the third-session ranking is 'August 6, 2026' in the call and 'by 7 August 2026' on the webpage. 5) TRACK vs. STANDALONE PROGRAMME: Computer Science is not a separate accredited degree - it is the English percorso of the single L-31 degree whose Italian track is called 'Informatica'. They share one admission call, one degree class and one webpage, but have separate seat quotas and separate ranking lists, and the English track has its own language rules. The programme card therefore shows 'LANGUAGE: English Italian'. 6) DUPLICATE OFFICIAL URLS: corsi.unitn.it serves the same programme at /en/computer-science-bachelor and at /en/computer-sciences (the latter is the link used from the DISI site); /en/computer-science is the Master's degree. The canonical bachelor URL used in the menu and breadcrumb is /en/computer-science-bachelor. 7) REQUIRED DOCUMENTS is marked uncertain because UniTrento publishes no single checklist for this programme; the list given is assembled from Note 2 and Note 3 of the call plus the language-certificate page, and additional documents may be requested by the International Mobility Office during visa/pre-enrolment. 8) NUMBER OF NON-EU SCHOLARSHIPS for this programme is not published in advance - it is announced together with the ranking. 9) No IELTS/TOEFL minimum score is published for this bachelor: the B2 requirement is satisfied post-admission via the CLA test or a recognised certificate, so applicants without a certificate are not blocked at application stage.
